page: Vultr voc-m-16c-128gb-800s-amd is a memory-oriented server in the Optimized Cloud Compute family, configured with 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores and 128 GB of system memory. Powered by the AMD EPYC processor platform on the x86_64 architecture running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz, the instance delivers an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Cache resources include 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. Local high-speed persistence is provided by an integrated 800 GB NVMe solid-state drive, accompanied by one complimentary public IPv4 address. The server operates without discrete graphics hardware.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-core and memory sub-tier execution. The processor achieves top-tier performance in stress-ng single-core tests, complemented by strong rankings in PassMark memory testing and lightweight large language model text generation. Multi-threaded evaluations, including Geekbench multi-core, PassMark CPU benchmarks, and stress-ng multi-core suites, sit within the middle tiers. Memory throughput delivers 135.4 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 68.38 GB/sec for uncached writes, enabling steady performance for data handling and concurrent system utilities.

The 1:8 compute-to-memory ratio coupled with dedicated CPU allocations provides stable resource isolation, avoiding the unpredictability of burstable platforms. The integrated 800 GB NVMe drive offers high local throughput without the latency overhead of network-attached block devices. However, applications requiring advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 or AMX will find limited hardware vector acceleration, as the platform is capped at standard AVX. Additionally, the moderate base clock rate trades peak multi-threaded throughput for high memory density per core.

This hardware balance serves memory-intensive workloads that rely on low-latency local storage. Target deployments include in-memory key-value stores like Redis, relational database management systems, data caching layers, enterprise backend services, and lightweight CPU-based language model inference pipelines.
description: Vultr voc-m-16c-128gb-800s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance equipped with 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 AMD EPYC physical cores running at 2.0 GHz. Designed with a generous 1:8 vCPU-to-memory allocation, it integrates 128 GB of RAM and 800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. The x86_64 platform achieves top-tier single-core CPU throughput and strong memory benchmark rankings, alongside dependable multi-core processing speeds. Memory bandwidth registers at 135.4 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 68.38 GB/sec for writes. The absence of a dedicated GPU and AVX-512 extensions makes it less suitable for heavy matrix acceleration, yet its high memory density and dedicated core profile provide stable, cost-efficient scaling for memory-bound applications. The configuration is well suited for in-memory caching layers, relational databases, web application backends, and lightweight machine learning inference.
